comments.headline: Trees lack species, compatibility, and height documentation
comments.summary: Landscape plan shows trees with generic regulatory symbols but lacks species identification, utility compatibility (UC) designation per ECM Appendix F, and mature height information required to verify electrical clearance compliance.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy will review UC designations and may need to verify species compatibility once plan is updated
comments.attn: Confirm ECM Appendix F as the governing reference for UC column, mature height classifications, and large tree definition (40+ feet)

details.text: Trees on landscape plan identified only by regulatory category (M, SY, PL, P) without species names; plant species listed separately on Sheet 35 schedule without cross-reference to landscape plan locations

runComments.comment: The landscape plan identifies trees only by regulatory category (M, ST, PL, P) without species names. The plant schedule lists species using different symbols with no cross-reference to the landscape plan. A unified plant legend must be provided on the landscape plan identifying each tree location by species name (common and/or scientific) to allow verification of utility compatibility and mature height characteristics near electric facilities.

Landscape plan (Sheet 31) uses generic tree symbols (circles labeled with M, SY, PL, P designations) without species identification. Plant species names are listed separately on Sheet 35 plant schedule but are not identified on the landscape plan drawing itself, preventing verification of species placement relative to electrical infrastructure.

details.text: Proposed trees within 15 feet of overhead electric distribution lines lack utility-compatible (UC) designation per ECM Appendix F. Species include Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Mexican Redbud; cannot verify code compliance without UC designation.

runComments.comment: Trees are proposed within 15 feet of overhead electric distribution lines (some as close as 3-5 feet), but species are not identified at these locations on the landscape plan, making it impossible to verify utility compatibility. Applicant must identify species at each tree location and confirm utility-compatible status per ECM Appendix F, or provide documented Austin Energy approval.

Landscape plan shows trees (mitigation trees and existing trees) located directly adjacent to or overlapping the OHE line along the southern boundary. Plant schedule does not identify utility-compatible status per ECM Appendix F UC column for any of the proposed trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Mexican Redbud). Without documented utility compatibility designation and without clearance dimensions on the plans, compliance cannot be verified.

Proposed tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) are listed on plant schedule but utility-compatible (UC) designation cannot be verified without reference to ECM Appendix F UC column. Compliance with non-utility-compatible tree restriction within 15 feet of distribution conductors cannot be determined.

details.text: Mature heights not provided for proposed species near overhead electric distribution lines (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel); only minimum planting specifications shown. Cannot verify whether trees qualify as "large" (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) requiring 25-foot clearance from conductors.

runComments.comment: Mature heights for proposed tree species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) are not provided. Only planting specs show minimum installation heights (16' or 8-10'). Cannot verify whether proposed trees will mature to 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F definition. Applicant must provide mature height information for all species proposed within 25 feet of overhead lines.

Landscape plan shows shade trees (Live Oak and Cedar Elm, each with minimum 16-foot planting specification) proposed near the OHE line on the southern boundary. However, plant schedule does not specify mature heights per ECM Appendix F, which is required to determine if trees qualify as 'large' (40+ feet mature height) subject to the 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors. Mature height from ECM Appendix F cannot be verified.

Plant specifications on Sheet 35 show minimum purchase height (e.g., '16 HT MINIMUM' for Cedar Elm and Live Oak) but not mature height per ECM Appendix F. Cannot verify if proposed trees meet large tree definition (40+ feet mature height) needed to evaluate this restriction.

details.text: Landscape plan does not differentiate or designate which trees are large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F). Plant schedule shows only minimum purchase specifications, not mature height classifications needed to determine applicable clearance rules.

runComments.comment: No mature height information is provided for proposed tree species. The landscape plan contains no notation indicating which trees will mature to large size (40+ feet). Applicant must provide mature heights for all proposed species per ECM Appendix F and clearly designate large trees on the landscape plan with a distinct symbol or notation.

Landscape plan (Sheet 31) and plant schedule (Sheet 35) do not differentiate large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) from smaller species. The plant schedule shows only minimum planting specifications (16' for Live Oak and Cedar Elm) without reference to their ECM Appendix F mature height classifications. Without this designation, it is not possible to verify whether clearance requirements for large trees near overhead facilities are being met.

Landscape plan does not differentiate or designate which trees are large (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F). Plant specifications on Sheet 35 show minimum purchase sizes only (e.g., '16 HT MINIMUM' for shade trees) rather than mature height classifications needed for electrical clearance verification.

details.text: Transmission infrastructure referenced on Sheet 3 with 50-foot lateral clearance requirement. Proposed tree species lack UC designation verification per ECM Appendix F. Actual lateral distances from transmission conductors cannot be precisely measured from submitted plans.

runComments.comment: Transmission infrastructure referenced in Sheet 3 general notes with stricter 25-foot clearance requirement. Proposed tree species lack UC designation verification per ECM Appendix F. Actual lateral distances from transmission conductors cannot be precisely measured from submitted plans.

details.text: Mature height per ECM Appendix F cannot be determined from submitted plant specifications for trees near transmission structures. Actual lateral distances from transmission conductors cannot be precisely measured. Compliance with large tree (40+ feet) clearance requirement (50 lateral feet from transmission conductors) cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Mature height per ECM Appendix F cannot be determined from submitted plant specifications. Actual lateral distances from transmission structures cannot be precisely measured. Compliance cannot be verified.

comments.headline: Tree clearances to poles, pads, and lines not verified
comments.summary: Trees are positioned adjacent to utility poles, transformer pads, and overhead electric lines without documented clearance distances on plans or required Austin Energy approval for non-compliant placements.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy approval required for any trees within restricted electrical clearance zones
comments.attn: Vision analysis and sheet comparison confirm tree positions relative to utility infrastructure; precise measurement challenges noted by reviewers

details.text: Tree proposed 3-5 feet from utility pole on western property boundary at southwest corner. Minimum clearance requirement is 10 feet per UCM § 1.10.10.4; tree must be relocated or documented Austin Energy approval provided.

runComments.comment: A tree is proposed 3-5 feet from a utility pole on the western property boundary. This violates the 10-foot minimum clearance required by UCM § 1.10.10.4. Applicant must either relocate this tree beyond 10 feet from the pole or provide documented Austin Energy approval for the variance.

Overhead electric poles are present along the OHE line (shown on Sheet 21 and Sheet 31). Trees are shown on the landscape plan in proximity to these utility areas. However, the landscape plan does not dimension the clearance distances between individual trees and specific poles. Without clearance dimensions, the 10-foot minimum separation requirement cannot be verified.

Vision analysis confirms tree symbols are positioned in corner areas where utility poles are located. Exact lateral distances cannot be measured from available plans. Clearance verification requires precise measurement not provided on landscape plan.

details.text: Multiple trees shown directly above or adjacent to pad-mounted transformer equipment at five locations (northwest, mid-west, southwest, south-central, east). Ten-foot minimum clearance not documented; tree canopies overlap transformer pads on Sheet 31.

runComments.comment: Multiple proposed trees are shown directly above or within immediate proximity to electrical transformer pads on the site. This suggests non-compliance with the 10-foot clearance requirement from pad-mounted equipment. Applicant must provide clear distance dimensions and confirm all trees are at least 10 feet from each transformer pad, or provide Austin Energy approval.

Sheet 21 electrical design plan shows a pad-mounted transformer in the western street yard area. Sheet 31 landscape plan shows a street yard tree (marked SY) in the same general area with the tree's canopy circle drawn extremely close to or overlapping the transformer pad. No clearance dimension is provided. Minimum 10-foot clearance from tree trunk to pad-mounted equipment cannot be verified from available evidence.

Four electrical transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 (west side near Bldg 1-2 and 8; east side near Bldg 4-5 and 6-7). Landscape plan shows trees in these general areas but precise lateral distances from equipment access doors and pad edges cannot be verified.

details.text: Landscape plan shows overhead electric (OHE) line and trees on same drawing (Sheet 31) but lacks dimensioned clearance measurements between tree trunk centers and conductor line. Trees with canopies overlapping OHE line position cannot be verified as compliant without clearance dimensions.

runComments.comment: While the landscape plan does show the OHE utility line and trees in relation to it (both are depicted on Sheet 31), the plan fails to demonstrate compliance because no clearance dimensions are provided between tree trunk centers and the conductor line. Trees shown with canopies overlapping the OHE line position lack any dimensioned clearance verification. Reviewer cannot verify clearance compliance from the presented evidence.

Landscape plan shows both tree symbols and overhead electric (OHE) line on the same drawing but lacks sufficient documentation to verify clearances. Vision analysis identified trees positioned directly on or immediately adjacent to OHE line markings on southern boundary, with no dimensions, callouts, or notes confirming clearance compliance. Cross-reference to electrical plan (Sheet 21) required for clearance verification is not explicitly shown.

details.text: No Austin Energy written approval provided for trees within electrical clearance zones. Sheet 3 Block 13 prohibits trees within 25 feet of transmission structure base. Landscape shows trees in restricted zones requiring approval or relocation.

runComments.comment: Trees are proposed within clearance zones that violate UCM § 1.10.10.4 minimums (less than 15 feet from distribution, less than 10 feet from poles). No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing these variances is evident in the submitted plans or supplementary documents. Applicant must either relocate trees to comply with clearance requirements, or provide documented Austin Energy written approval for the proposed variance.

The landscape plan shows trees positioned adjacent to or overlapping the OHE line along the southern boundary and near the transformer pad in the street yard, but no documented written approval from Austin Energy is included in the submitted plans or supplementary documents authorizing these tree placements within the restricted electrical clearance zones. Without such approval, trees in these proximity zones constitute a regulatory violation.

Sheet 3 Block 13 explicitly states 'No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' Landscape plan shows trees along western boundary near transmission infrastructure. No Austin Energy written approval letter is referenced or provided in submitted documents authorizing trees within this prohibited clearance zone.

comments.headline: Underground equipment locations and root barriers not shown
comments.summary: Underground electrical equipment locations are not clearly identified on landscape plan, preventing verification of 5-foot clearances and 4-foot root barrier specifications required by UCM § 1.10.10.4.
comments.crossDep: Electrical and landscaping plans must be coordinated to identify all underground equipment and clearances
comments.attn: Sheet 21 shows underground lines and pull boxes; confirm all underground equipment is identified on landscape plan with clearance dimensions and root barrier details on Sheet 37

details.text: Underground electric lines marked as '- E -' on Sheet 31 but specific locations of underground equipment (pull boxes, vaults, buried transformers) are not clearly identified. Without identified equipment locations and dimensioned clearances, the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Underground electric lines are shown on the landscape plan (marked as '- E -' on Sheet 31). However, the specific locations of underground electric equipment (pull boxes, vaults, buried transformers, etc.) are not clearly identified on the landscape plan. Without identified equipment locations and without dimensioned clearances, the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified.

Underground electric lines and pull boxes are shown on Sheet 21 electrical plan. Landscape plan shows trees throughout site but no clearance measurements documented to verify 5-foot minimum distance from underground equipment.

details.text: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) and landscape details (Sheet 37) do not show root barrier specifications. No 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from underground equipment are detailed or dimensioned. Equipment locations must be identified on landscape plan to determine which trees within 20-foot proximity zone require root barriers.

runComments.comment: Underground electric equipment locations are not clearly identified on the landscape plan. Therefore, it cannot be determined which proposed trees fall within the 20-foot proximity zone requiring root barriers. Additionally, no root barrier specifications are shown on the landscape plan or in the landscape notes. Without identified equipment locations and without documented root barrier specifications, compliance cannot be verified.

Landscape plan (Sheet 31) and landscape details (Sheet 37) do not show root barrier specifications. No 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from underground equipment are detailed or dimensioned on the landscape plans.
